Caching slow work

Source: vignettes/caching-slow-work.Rmd
caching-slow-work.Rmd

Most code that wants a cache has the same shape: a function that is slow, called again with arguments it has seen before, by more than one session. This article walks through that case, from a function that calls a web service to the files it downloads.

library(dastash)
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "slow-work")
s <- stash(dir)

A slow function

Here is a stand-in for a call to a web service: it takes a moment, and its answer depends only on its arguments. calls counts how often it really runs.

calls <- 0
fetch_rates <- function(base, date) {
  calls <<- calls + 1
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
  set.seed(as.integer(date))
  data.frame(
    currency = c("EUR", "USD", "JPY"),
    rate = round(runif(3, 0.5, 150), 4)
  )
}

stash_memoise() wraps it. Rates for a past date do not change, but give them a day’s expiry anyway, and a tag to drop them all by:

rates <- stash_memoise(
  fetch_rates,
  s,
  expire = as.difftime(1, units = "days"),
  tags = "rates"
)

system.time(rates("CHF", as.Date("2026-10-30")))
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>   0.004   0.000   0.534
system.time(rates("CHF", as.Date("2026-10-30")))
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>   0.001   0.001   0.001
calls
#> [1] 1

The second call is read from the stash. Each call is one entry, under a key made from the function’s name and its arguments:

rates("CHF", as.Date("2026-10-29"))
#>   currency    rate
#> 1      EUR 40.4205
#> 2      USD  7.2563
#> 3      JPY  2.1548
stash_keys(s, prefix = "fetch_rates/")
#> [1] "fetch_rates/v1/{base=s:CHF,date=d:2026-10-29}"
#> [2] "fetch_rates/v1/{base=s:CHF,date=d:2026-10-30}"

Results outlive the session

The entries are on disk, not in this session. Close the stash, open it again, and memoise the function again under the same name, as a new session or a scheduled job would: the answers are already there.

stash_close(s)
s <- stash(dir)
rates <- stash_memoise(fetch_rates, s, name = "fetch_rates")

rates("CHF", as.Date("2026-10-30"))
#>   currency     rate
#> 1      EUR  19.6596
#> 2      USD  32.5869
#> 3      JPY 149.9198
calls
#> [1] 2

Every process on the machine that opens dir shares them the same way: a Shiny app and a nightly job that fills it, or parallel workers that each compute part of the work and read what the others computed.

When the answers change

There are three ways to throw results away, from narrow to wide.

# One call.
stash_forget(rates, "CHF", as.Date("2026-10-30"))

# Everything tagged when it was stored.
stash_evict(s, tag = "rates")
stash_keys(s, prefix = "fetch_rates/")
#> character(0)

When the function itself changes meaning, a new version gives it new keys. The old entries are no longer read, and leave as they expire or as the size limit evicts them.

rates <- stash_memoise(fetch_rates, s, name = "fetch_rates", version = 2)
stash_memoise_key(rates, "CHF", as.Date("2026-10-30"))
#> [1] "fetch_rates/v2/{base=s:CHF,date=d:2026-10-30}"

Files you download

Some slow work produces a file: a download, an export from another tool. codec_file() stores the file itself, and reading the entry gives a path to a read-only copy that every process shares.

download <- function(url) {
  # A stand-in for utils::download.file(url, path).
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  utils::write.csv(mtcars, path, row.names = FALSE)
  path
}

cached_download <- function(s, url) {
  path <- stash_get(s, url, default = NULL)
  if (is.null(path)) {
    tmp <- download(url)
    stash_set(s, url, tmp, codec = codec_file(), expire = 7 * 24 * 3600)
    unlink(tmp)
    path <- stash_get(s, url)
  }
  path
}

path <- cached_download(s, "https://example.org/mtcars.csv")
basename(path)
#> [1] "450a97ba6b438c6ea5bdf2aaac7eab0ecbbf812b5ff74b56f62dcf0a0c7eb0e5.csv"
nrow(utils::read.csv(path))
#> [1] 32

The file keeps its extension, so tools that go by it read it as they would the original.

Code written for cachem

Packages that take a cachem cache, such as memoise and Shiny’s bindCache(), can store in a stash through as_cachem():

cache <- as_cachem(s)
slow_square <- function(x) {
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
  x^2
}
fast_square <- memoise::memoise(slow_square, cache = cache)

system.time(fast_square(12))
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>   0.002   0.000   0.502
system.time(fast_square(12))
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>   0.010   0.000   0.011
stash_close(s)
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
